Count it when the item makes a derivative tool's record point to sc-agent for a shared rule instead of stating it, removes a restated shared rule from a derivative tool's record, or moves a shared rule into sc-agent's records. Merely not restating a rule, describing a tool's own behaviour, rewording sc-agent's text, or mentioning records is not stating it.

criteria.yes: The item makes a derivative tool's record defer to sc-agent for a shared rule, removes a restated shared rule from such a record, or consolidates a shared rule in sc-agent's records.
criteria.no: The item does none of these: it is silent on where shared rules live, describes only a tool's own behaviour, rewords text without moving or removing a restatement, restates a shared rule, or is about something else.
criteria.unclear: The item touches shared rules and derivative tool records, but whether it makes them single-sourced in sc-agent cannot be told.

contradicted.instructions: Would doing what `item.text` describes put a rule that applies to every decidr-based tool (logging, log root, model resolution, consent, retries, result-line fields and the like) into the records of a derivative tool such as judge-jev or plan-anchor, by restating, copying or redefining it there? Stating the tool's own behaviour, pointing to sc-agent, editing sc-agent's own records, changing code, or saying nothing about shared rules is not a violation.

criteria.yes: The item restates, copies or redefines a shared decidr-tool rule in a derivative tool's records.
criteria.no: The item does not put a shared rule into a derivative tool's records: it defers to sc-agent, states only the tool's own behaviour, edits sc-agent's records, changes no records, or is silent.
criteria.unclear: The item may add shared-rule text to a derivative tool's record, but the text does not make clear whether it does.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` say that a derivative decidr-based tool's records defer to sc-agent for a shared rule (logging, model resolution and the like), or remove or move a shared rule so that only sc-agent's records state it? Silence about shared rules is not presence.

criteria.yes: The item points a derivative tool's records to sc-agent for a shared rule, or removes or moves a restated shared rule so sc-agent's records are its only source.
criteria.no: The item does not do that: it is silent, covers only the tool's own behaviour, rewords text in place, copies a shared rule, or is about something else.
criteria.unclear: It is impossible to tell whether the item makes sc-agent the only source of the shared rule.

contradicted.instructions: Would doing what `item.text` describes put a rule that applies to every decidr-based tool (logging, log root, model resolution, consent, retries, result-line fields and the like) into the records of a derivative tool such as judge-jev or plan-anchor, by restating, copying or redefining it there? Stating the tool's own behaviour, pointing to sc-agent, editing sc-agent's own records, changing code, or saying nothing about shared rules is not a violation.

criteria.yes: The item restates, copies or redefines a shared decidr-tool rule in a derivative tool's records.
criteria.no: The item does not put a shared rule into a derivative tool's records: it defers to sc-agent, states only the tool's own behaviour, edits sc-agent's records, changes no records, or is silent.
criteria.unclear: The item may add shared-rule text to a derivative tool's record, but the text does not make clear whether it does.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` describe work that matches at least one of these signals: (1) it adds or edits a REQ, NFR or ADR record of judge-jev, plan-anchor or another decidr-based tool (for example REQ-JEV-*, or files under docs/requirements/, docs/nfr/, docs/adr/ or docs/<crate>/requirements/); (2) it adds, moves or rewords record text about log placement or log root, model resolution, consent, retries or result-line fields; (3) it adds or edits an sc-agent record that states a rule for all decidr-based tools. Judge only what the item says it will change. Code changes, tests, bug fixes and reading or reviewing records do not match, even when they mention logging, retries, model resolution or a tool's records.

criteria.yes: The item adds, edits, moves or rewords text in a record as described by signal (1), (2) or (3).
criteria.no: The item changes no REQ, NFR or ADR record text: it changes code, tests, dependencies or configuration, fixes a bug, or only reads or mentions records or logging.
criteria.unclear: The item may change record text matching a signal, but the text does not say whether any record text is changed.

anchor.statement: A rule that applies to every decidr-based tool (logging, model resolution and the like) must be specified only in sc-agent's records; a derivative tool's records (judge-jev, plan-anchor and others) must not restate it and give only the tool name and the tool's own behaviour, so each rule has one source.
anchor.scope: adds or edits a REQ, NFR or ADR record of judge-jev, plan-anchor or another decidr-based tool (e.g. REQ-JEV-*, files under docs/requirements/, docs/nfr/, docs/adr/ or docs/<crate>/requirements/); adds, moves or rewords text about log placement or log root, model resolution, consent, retries or result-line fields in any record; adds or edits an sc-agent record that states a rule for all decidr-based tools

criteria.yes: The item adds or changes REQ, NFR or ADR record text and the change matches signal (1), (2) or (3): a derivative decidr-based tool's record, record text about log placement, log root, model resolution, consent, retries or result-line fields, or an sc-agent record stating a rule for all decidr-based tools.
criteria.no: The item adds or changes no REQ, NFR or ADR record text (for example a code change, a test, a dependency bump, a bug fix, or reading records), or it changes a record that matches none of the signals.
criteria.unclear: The item may change a record, but whether it does, or which record, cannot be told from the text.

anchor.statement: A rule that applies to every decidr-based tool (logging, model resolution and the like) must be specified only in sc-agent's records; a derivative tool's records (judge-jev, plan-anchor and others) must not restate it and give only the tool name and the tool's own behaviour, so each rule has one source.
anchor.scope: adds or edits a REQ, NFR or ADR record of judge-jev, plan-anchor or another decidr-based tool (e.g. REQ-JEV-*, files under docs/requirements/, docs/nfr/, docs/adr/ or docs/<crate>/requirements/); adds, moves or rewords text about log placement or log root, model resolution, consent, retries or result-line fields in any record; adds or edits an sc-agent record that states a rule for all decidr-based tools

item.title: irrelevant-retry-code
item.text: Change the retry back-off in crates/sc-jev-client/src/retry.rs from a fixed 2 s wait to exponential back-off; no requirement, NFR or ADR text changes.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` say that a derivative decidr-based tool's records defer to sc-agent for a shared rule (logging, model resolution and the like), or remove or move a shared rule so that only sc-agent's records state it? Silence about shared rules is not presence.

criteria.yes: The item points a derivative tool's records to sc-agent for a shared rule, or removes or moves a restated shared rule so sc-agent's records are its only source.
criteria.no: The item does not do that: it is silent, covers only the tool's own behaviour, rewords text in place, copies a shared rule, or is about something else.
criteria.unclear: It is impossible to tell whether the item makes sc-agent the only source of the shared rule.

contradicted.instructions: Would doing what `item.text` describes put a rule that applies to every decidr-based tool (logging, log root, model resolution, consent, retries, result-line fields and the like) into the records of a derivative tool such as judge-jev or plan-anchor, by restating, copying or redefining it there? criteria.unclear: The item may add shared-rule text to a derivative tool's record, but the text does not make clear whether it does.
